articles.title: Texans vs. Titans game in Week 5 is so bad that even The Weather Channel is dunking on it
articles.summary: No one is interested in a Week 5 battle between two winless teams.
articles.body:
What happens when you pit two miserable and directionless 0-4 teams against each other in Week 5 of the NFL season? You get a game so bad even The Weather Channel is dunking on it.

The Houston Texans and the Tennessee Titans will square off in Week 5 in a game that should — barring a tie — give one of those teams their first win of the 2026 season. If you're not a fan of either team, watching the contest is a tough sell. The Titans haven't shown much improvement in Cam Ward's second season and the Texans' previously excellent defense has proven vulnerable.

Because of that, the NFL Memes account tried to shoot out an easy joke suggesting the game should be flexed to The Weather Channel, as a national audience shouldn't be subjected to the contest.

There was just one problem with that joke: Even The Weather Channel has no interest in airing Texans vs. Titans.

That's … pretty bleak. If The Weather Channel has no interest in broadcasting a bad NFL game, how can CBS hope to salvage the contest?

It should be obvious, but the whole thing is pretty clearly a joke. But with sporting events suddenly split between seemingly every available network and streaming service, it's worth pointing out that The Weather Channel is one of the few networks that does not own broadcast rights to NFL games. Given the state of television and streaming in 2026, though, we can't rule out a future NFL broadcast on the network.

While the Titans do seem stuck in the mud, there is some hope the Texans turn things around. The team has played some strong offenses thus far, perhaps explaining why the defense has seemingly taken a step back so far.

A possible get-right game against the Titans could get the Texans back on track. And while an 0-4 record will be tough to overcome, there is some precedent for a massive turnaround. The 1992 San Diego Chargers managed to rally from an 0-4 start to make the playoffs.

They are the only team to pull off that feat, however, so the Texans would have a lot of work to do if the team managed to win in Week 5.

articles.title: Sean McVay Says Rams Coaches Have to 'Get the Hell Out of the Way' After Sideline Penalty vs. Eagles
articles.summary: After a member of his staff committed a rare gaffe in Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay accepted responsibility for the mistake.
articles.body:
After a member of his staff committed a rare gaffe in Sunday's win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay accepted responsibility for the mistake.

Rams quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone was called for a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for standing too close to the field when an official who was running down the sideline collided with him. McVay said he and his staff deserve criticism just as much as his players receive when they commit penalties.

"Focus, concentration and situational awareness, we have to do a better job on that," McVay said, per Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk. "When it rains, it pours. Shoot, we're getting penalties on our staff now too. Thank God we won that one. Rags would have never lived that one down. He felt bad about that one. So he took great accountability. We'll get everybody the hell out of the way. And I need to get the hell out of the way as well."

In all, the Rams were flagged eight times for 100 penalty yards. Still, they managed to escape with a 24-20 win following an impressive fourth-quarter comeback.

McVay and the Rams (2-2) will try to stay focused as they prepare for a tough matchup against the Buffalo Bills (3-1) on Monday Night Football in Week 5.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady are practically identical in this wild career stat after Chiefs' latest win
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs beat the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 on Sunday to move to 4-0, and Patrick Mahomes keeps getting held up against Tom Brady.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs beat the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 on Sunday to move to 4-0, and Patrick Mahomes keeps getting held up against Tom Brady. This time the comparison is hard to wave away. Through 150 career starts, both quarterbacks were level at 115-35. Mahomes, 31, is back from the ACL tear that ended his last season, and the early results suggest the knee isn't slowing him. The Chiefs have a bye week next, which gives everyone time to argue about what the matching records really mean.How similar are Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady's records after 150 starts?Almost mirror images. Mahomes and Brady are both 98-31 in 129 regular-season starts. Each went 5-2 across seven AFC Championship Game appearances. Each also has the same Super Bowl record through the same number of trips, 3-2 in five appearances. That is team success lined up almost game for game.The passing numbers tell a different story. Across their first nine seasons, Mahomes threw for 35,655 yards and 267 touchdowns. Brady had 26,440 and 197. Mahomes also ran for 2,655 yards in that span, against 533 for Brady. The results match, but the routes do not.Sunday was a reminder that Mahomes does not need big numbers to win. He completed 15 of 30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tyquan Thornton. Thornton finished with 111 yards on five catches. Kenneth Walker III did the heavy lifting on the ground, running for 177 yards and two scores. Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards for Las Vegas, so Kansas City had to earn it. The Chiefs scored 20 points in the fourth quarter, and the Raiders' defense had not allowed any fourth-quarter points all season before that. Thornton later left with what looked like a serious lower-body injury.Can Patrick Mahomes catch Tom Brady's career totals?The wins are not the hard part. Longevity is. Brady played 23 seasons and finished with more than 89,000 passing yards, and Mahomes is nowhere close to that yet. He is 31 and in his tenth season, so the math only works if his body cooperates. The knee injury showed how much depends on health. Staying sharp into your 40s is a separate challenge, and nobody can predict it.The rings are the other gap. Mahomes has three. Brady retired with seven, and he won the last one against Mahomes in Super Bowl 55. articles.title: NFL Refs Association to 'Challenge the Severity' of Adrian Hill, Jeff Seeman Suspensions
articles.summary: The NFL Referees Association is challenging the suspensions given to Adrian Hill and Jeff Seeman following Week 4.
articles.body:
The NFL Referees Association is challenging the suspensions given to Adrian Hill and Jeff Seeman following Week 4.

In a statement released on Tuesday, the NFLRA announced it will "challenge the severity" of the NFL's discipline for both officials by meeting with the league's officiating department.

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

The statement also states the NFLRA plans to meet with leaders from the NFL Players Association to "address on-field conduct and the growing levels of confrontation between players and officials."

NFL vice president of officiating Ramon George announced on Monday that Seeman (two games) and Hill (one game) were suspended for instances of unprofessional conduct during the games they were working in Week 4.

Seeman was seen yelling at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride in the fourth quarter of their game against the New York Giants.

Hill, who was working the Miami Dolphins-Minnesota Vikings game, was inadvertently knocked down when Vikings linebacker Eric Wilson collided with him.

Wilson attempted to help Hill up, but Hill stood up on his own and had an animated reaction toward the Vikings linebacker.

In response to the incident with Seeman and McBride, NFLPA executive director JC Tretter wrote on X that Seeman's behavior is "unacceptable" and urged the same standard for players be applied to the refs.

"Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed," Tretter wrote. "We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Per Shanna McCarriston of CBS Sports, the NFL had not suspended a referee since December 2018 when umpire Roy Ellison was placed on administrative leave.

Seeman started as an NFL referee in 2002 as both a field judge and line judge. He has worked exclusively as a line judge since 2003 and is listed as having worked 380 games in his career, per Pro Football Reference .

Hill's first season in the NFL was in 2010 as a side judge and line judge. He has worked 117 games as a referee since the 2019 season.

articles.summary: The reigning Super Bowl champions aren't adding veteran help to their running back room after all.
articles.body:
The reigning Super Bowl champions aren't adding veteran help to their running back room after all.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Seattle Seahawks "decided not to" sign Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he underwent a physical.

ESPN's Brady Henderson reported the Seahawks now plan to sign running back Robert Henry Jr. off the Washington Commanders' practice squad.

Running back depth has become an area of concern for the Seahawks in the early going this season. Most notably, rookie Jadarian Price will miss at least four games on IR because of a chest injury.

"This is just what happens in football. Unfortunately, injuries happen," head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters . "He can't control these things. He's done everything we've asked him to do since he got here. He's had a great attitude. He's been a great teammate. He has a great future. He's going to play great football for us when he comes back, whenever that is ... It's just unfortunate."

As for Zach Charbonnet, he is yet to play this season as he recovers from a torn ACL. However, Seattle opened his 21-day practice window on Thursday, suggesting he could be nearing his return.

With both of them out for Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers, Emanuel Wilson thrived in the primary running back role. He finished with 21 carries for 81 yards and one touchdown to go with three catches for 39 yards and another score.

Backup George Holani tallied seven carries for 18 yards.

Mixon played seven seasons for the Cincinnati Bengals and surpassed the 1,000-yard mark on the ground four times, including when he was a Pro Bowler in 2021. He was also a Pro Bowler in 2024 with the Texans when he ran for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns.

The 30-year-old missed the 2025 campaign because of a foot injury. Houston released him in March.

articles.body:

Gardner-Johnson shared a meme on social media the day after Patriots coach Mike Vrabel trolled him in a radio show appearance.

The exchange started when Gardner-Johnson made a postgame comment about wide receiver Efton Chism III, who used one hand to haul down his game-winning touchdown catch in the Patriots' 29-26 Week 4 win.

"An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won't hear from him again... A practice-squad player made a hell of a play," Gardner-Johnson said about Chism after Sunday's loss.

Vrabel was then asked about Gardner-Johnson's comments in a Monday appearance on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show.

"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said about Gardner-Johnson.

Chism has been a member of the Patriots since he made the 53-man roster as an undrafted free agent in 2025. Gardner-Johnson has made regular-season appearances for six teams over eight seasons.

articles.title: 3 of Nolan Wells' Friends Sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for Defamation
articles.summary: JACKSON, Miss. (AP) — Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Black college student who went missing from a Mississippi island during a Fourth of July celebration and was later found dead, are suing NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.
articles.body:
JACKSON, Miss. (AP) — Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Black college student who went missing from a Mississippi island during a Fourth of July celebration and was later found dead, are suing NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

Lawyers for the friends said they intend to file several more defamation claims this week against content creators and have previously indicated their intent to sue the Rev. Al Sharpton and "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin for comments they made while discussing Wells' death.

The fathers of the three friends, who are under 21 and considered minors under Mississippi law, filed the federal lawsuit Monday on their behalf.

The lawsuit alleges Owens defamed the three friends after posting on X: "ARREST THEM IMMEDIATELY!!" Owens' post also linked to an Instagram video, which theorized the three friends killed Wells and tampered with his phone, according to the lawsuit. The post was made days after a Mississippi grand jury declined to recommend charges in Wells' death.

Owens has 1.2 million followers on X and had previously pledged $25,000 to a reward fund for information leading to an arrest and conviction in Wells' death.

"Not only is he defaming them, he's basically saying to the mob, get your pitchforks, get your torches," said Edward Paltzik, a defamation and media attorney representing the three friends.

The Associated Press attempted to contact Owens through social media and SMAC Entertainment, which, according to its website, manages Owens, but did not immediately receive a response.

The three were part of a group of 30 friends, including Wells, who rode to Horn Island on three boats on the Fourth of July. Wells' friends said Wells did not return to the mainland with them, choosing instead to stay behind to talk with a girl, a claim his family has disputed. His body was found two days later off the island's coast.

Both state and independent autopsies have not determined Wells' cause of death, though the grand jury found his death was "consistent with drowning." Wells' family and their lawyers disputed the grand jury's findings, pointing to unexplained bruising on the back of his head and noting that his airways and stomach were devoid of water.

Images showing Wells with white friends the day he went missing fueled online speculation that racial dynamics played a role in his death.

Two of the three friends who are suing Owens were singled out online in part because they appear in a photo with Wells and one other friend on a boat, which was circulated on social media after his disappearance. The third called Wells' mother and the U.S. Coast Guard to report Wells missing.

articles.title: Lane Johnson Announces Shocking Retirement During 14th NFL Season, Won 2 Super Bowls with Eagles
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles legend and offensive lineman Lane Johnson is retiring.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles legend and offensive lineman Lane Johnson is retiring.

Johnson took to social media Tuesday to announce his decision, which he called an "incredibly difficult" one.

"I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season," he wrote. "But after a lot of reflection, I've realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed.

"Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game. And right now my heart is telling me that it's time to say goodbye to football."

The Eagles reacted to the two-time Super Bowl champion's decision in what was his 14th season with the franchise:

Eagles chairman and CEO Jeffrey Lurie released a statement that called Johnson "an all-time Eagle and one of the best players ever to play his position in the NFL."

He also recognized Johnson for his contributions to the community and ended by saying, "We appreciate everything Lane has contributed to our organization, and we wish him and his family nothing but the best."

This comes after Johnson was a late scratch from Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams because of personal reasons .

Philadelphia is scheduled to fly to London on Friday for its upcoming game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and will now need Markel Bell to fill in at right tackle moving forward. Philadelphia selected Bell out of Miami with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft.

This is a golden opportunity for the rookie to start for a presumed playoff contender, although it is also a high-pressure one. He is being tasked with replacing a franchise legend and ideally keeping the offense afloat enough to bounce back from two straight losses.

As for Johnson, he surpassed even the highest of expectations that were put in place when the Eagles selected him with the No. 4 overall pick of the 2013 NFL draft.

His resume includes the two Super Bowl titles, two First-Team All-Pro selections and six Pro Bowl nods. He started 171 games for the NFC East team over his 14 seasons and remained effective well into his career.

In fact, he was a Pro Bowler and Second-Team All-Pro nod as recently as the 2024 campaign.

Johnson will forever be an Eagles legend and is certainly someone who could find himself in Canton, Ohio, one day as a Pro Football Hall of Famer.

But his retirement is an abrupt one in the middle of a season where he had returned to start for the Eagles. They will have to adjust on the fly against the Jaguars and the rest of their upcoming opponents as they look to battle for an NFC East crown.

articles.title: Vikings' KOC Talks 'Implications' of T.J. Hockenson Not Scoring TD amid Fantasy, Gambling Fallout
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings escaped Sunday's game with a 15-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but the final score would have looked better if T.J. Hockenson scored a touchdown instead of going down with two minutes remaining so they could kneel out the rest of the game.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings escaped Sunday's game with a 15-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins, but the final score would have looked better if T.J. Hockenson scored a touchdown instead of going down with two minutes remaining so they could kneel out the rest of the game.

Fantasy football managers and gamblers certainly took note, but head coach Kevin O'Connell praised the tight end for making the right football play and wasn't worried about those "implications" from elsewhere.

"We call that Rolex," he said during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show (9:25 mark). "That was the hardest Rolex decision to make since I've been a head coach. … We go in the end zone right there, you're probably looking at at least another potential two-minute drive where some really important players who have played a lot of football go back on the field for defense.

"… I told our offense, if you want to score, do it earlier. … That's part of our game. I'm not exactly hanging the 15-10 score on the mantle at home, but I will take a 4-0 season to start."

O'Connell's job is to put the Vikings in the best position to win both during the individual game and over the long course of the season. With that in mind, Hockenson going down so the offense can take a knee is the right play.

Not only does it rule out the unlikely possibility of Miami scoring, recovering an onside kick and scoring again, it also avoided any scenarios where the defense suffered an injury near the end of the game.

And keeping that defense, which has been largely dominant during a 4-0 start to the season, fresh will put the Vikings in the best position to succeed as the 2026 campaign continues.

Still, gamblers who wanted Minnesota to cover the spread or fantasy managers who wanted a touchdown from Hockenson surely aren't thrilled with how things played out.

After Mack Hollins suffered a calf injury against the Bills, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said the team could explore options at wide receiver. Could one of them be Tyreek Hill?

Hill wouldn't be an immediate fix, as he is finishing up his recovery from last year's major knee injury, but he could add an intriguing element to any offense down the stretch once he's ready to play.

As the Patriots weigh whether to add at the position, one insider explained why Hill wouldn't be the right fit for the Patriots.

Insider Explains Why Patriots Shouldn't Pursue Tyreek Hill

Speaking on "Zolak & Bertrand" on Tuesday, ESPN's Mike Reiss said he wouldn't pursue Hill if he were the Patriots.

"It would make me nervous, just everything around him," Reiss said, likely referring to the litany of off-field troubles that have followed Hill since his collegiate days. Hill is currently under NFL investigation for a Personal Conduct Policy violation after he was accused of domestic abuse in divorce filings in 2025, Pro Football Talk confirmed.

When pressed on the kind of impact Hill could make just by forcing defenses to cover him, Reiss was apprehensive that he could still put that kind of scare into teams at his age and coming off a significant knee injury.

When Scott Zolak said Hill's presence would make an opposing safety "nervous" because "you got to find [Hill], Reiss asked, "You still do?"

The kind of impact Hill can make after missing more than a year with multiple ligament years and a dislocated knee is a mystery that could make teams apprehensive as he prepares to return to the NFL. The Chiefs, however, already know Hill well and could be more willing to be patient with him, which has made Kansas City the top potential landing spot for the former All-Pro.

articles.title: Survey: Will the NY Giants win the NFC East?
articles.summary: Can the NY Giants go from worst to first in the NFC East?
articles.body:
The New York Giants have emerged from the first month of the 2026 season with a 3-1 record. That much isn't surprising and is in line with many preseason predictions.

What wasn't expected is that the Giants not only have sole possession of first place in the NFC East, but they've done it without Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns. Most expected the Giants to fold once they lost their franchise quarterback and star pass rusher. Instead, the Giants have kept fighting, literally down to the closing seconds of the last two games, and new stars have emerged.

Arvell Reese is positioning himself in the race for defensive rookie of the year, while Abdul Carter has been a devastating pass rusher. At the same time, Jevon Holland, Deonte Banks, and Greg Newsome II have been playing much better in the secondary than many expected.

Elsewhere in the NFC East, meanwhile, the other teams have issues. The Philadelphia Eagles are short-handed and a mess on offense. The Dallas Cowboys have one of the most potent offenses in the NFL, but a defense that is still porous. Finally, the Washington Commanders don't know what to expect from Jayden Daniels and there are questions elsewhere on their offense and defense.

So that brings up the question… Can the Giants stay resilient, hold off their division rivals, go from Worst To First, and win the NFC East?

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country.

articles.title: Lane Johnson retirement creates major fantasy concerns for Jalen Hurts, Eagles offense
articles.summary: Rookie Markel Bell inherits right tackle as Philadelphia's backfield thins out, with Saquon Barkley week-to-week and Tank Bigsby headed for core-muscle surge...
articles.body:
Lane Johnson's retirement strips the Philadelphia Eagles of their most dependable blocker four games into a season in which the offense already leads the NFL with 15 three-and-out drives , and the move lowers the outlook for every Philadelphia fantasy starter.

The 36-year-old right tackle announced Tuesday that he's stepping away after 14 seasons, two days removed from a late scratch for personal reasons. "Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health," Johnson wrote in his statement .

Johnson allowed two pressures, no sacks and no quarterback hits across 112 pass-blocking snaps this season. Since 2016, including the playoffs, the Eagles are 98-42-1 with the 2013 No. 4 overall pick in the lineup and 15-29 without him.

Markel Bell replaces Johnson at right tackle

Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Markel Bell (72) is seen against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. | Matt Marton-Imagn Images

Markel Bell is a third-round rookie taken 68th overall out of Miami. He made his first NFL start on short notice in the 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The 6-foot-9, 345-pound tackle is also switching sides, since 821 of his 826 snaps for the Hurricanes last season came at left tackle. Big fella makes his jersey look a size too small, even for a right tackle, a position known for its girth.

Bell didn't allow a sack across 440 pass-blocking snaps in his final college season. Head coach Nick Sirianni didn't single him out for any breakdowns against the Rams. "I thought he battled and went in there and played his butt off ," Sirianni said.

Behind him, 29-year-old swing tackle Fred Johnson hasn't logged an offensive snap this season because of a knee injury. That left the Eagles dressing only seven offensive linemen Sunday. A rookie starting full time behind an offense that went 0-for-12 on third down against the Rams makes every Eagles skill player a riskier weekly start.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) snaps the ball against the Los Angeles Rams | Bill Streicher-Imagn Images

What's a step down from bad? Terrible? Horrendous? Let's just call it Philly's 2026 offense with no Lane Johnson cause we got the preview, warts and all, last week.

Jalen Hurts threw for 93 yards on 12 completions against Los Angeles, his fewest passing yards in a game he started and finished. The Rams blitzed him on 60.6% of his dropbacks and generated pressure on 13 of their 18 blitzes.

Opponents will keep sending extra rushers at a first-year tackle. The former Oklahoma quarterback has taken 12 sacks through four games and has only 713 passing yards , so his fantasy value now rests on his 105 rushing yards on 21 carries and his goal-line work. I've got Hurts at QB15 for Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET game against the Jaguars in London. That might be too generous.

Eagles running backs and receivers outlook

Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (26) celebrates after a touchdown against the Washington Commanders | Bill Streicher-Imagn Images

Saquon Barkley is week-to-week with a hamstring injury suffered in the first quarter Sunday, and Tank Bigsby is headed to injured reserve after core-muscle surgery. That leaves Will Shipley as the only healthy running back on the active roster .

Barkley averaged 2.5 yards before contact on his 36 carries with Johnson in the lineup, and that early running room will be harder to find with a rookie on the right side. Shipley is a volume-based flex option if Barkley sits, but he has managed 51 yards on 15 carries this season.

DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and tight end Dallas Goedert both missed Week 4. Smith still leads the team with 19 catches for 235 yards on 27 targets. Dontayvion Wicks has 12 catches for 197 yards. Darius Cooper scored twice in the red zone against the Rams last week. More quick throws to protect Bell would favor Smith once he's healthy and keep Cooper in the flex conversation for deep leagues. Volume doesn't hurt, but a more one-dimensional offense hurts the team.

The entire Eagles offense, if it wasn't already, is on notice. Is it fair to downgrade the entire unit? It might be, and fantasy managers should err on the side of caution with everyone but the team's best players, like Barkley and Smith, when healthy. Even Goedert, when he returns, will be a borderline starter.

articles.title: As Eagles RT Lane Johnson announces retirement, one number captures his stunning impact
articles.summary: For years, presiding wisdom has said: If the NFL created an equivalent WAR metric, Johnson would pace the charts.
articles.body:
Despite its immense popularity, the NFL has never coined a statistic to rival baseball's wins above replacement (WAR) metric.

No one number tells a fan how valuable their team's roster member is, and certain positions in the NFL are far more difficult to quantify than others.

At the line of scrimmage, and particularly among offensive linemen and defensive tackles, basic football accounting barely scratches the surface of explaining a player's impact.

But for years, one split has defined Lane Johnson: the Eagles' record with vs. without him. As the six-time Pro Bowl right tackle announced his retirement Tuesday , that number seemed to speak loudly.

Johnson played 171 games for the Philadelphia Eagles from when they selected him fourth overall in the 2013 NFL Draft through last Monday's game at Chicago. The Eagles won a whopping 65.8% of those games (112-58-1) with Johnson anchoring their vaunted line.

Track the 46 games across those 13-plus seasons that Johnson hasn't played? The Eagles' win percentage plummets to 39.1% (18-28).

So for years, presiding wisdom has said: If the NFL created an equivalent WAR metric, Johnson would pace the charts.

Johnson, who has spoken publicly about his lingering mental health challenges, announced his retirement on Tuesday after missing the Eagles' Sunday loss to the Los Angeles Rams for what head coach Nick Sirianni described as "a personal matter."

He retires as a two-time first-team All-Pro and a two-time Super Bowl champion.

"Lane excelled under multiple coaching staffs, maintaining an elite level of play throughout his entire career," Eagles chairman and CEO Jeffrey Lurie said in a statement. "His combination of talent, strength, athleticism and intelligence made him a truly unique player in this league, and there is no doubt in my mind that one day he will be named to the Pro Football Hall of Fame."

The Eagles selected his expected successor, the 6-foot-9 Markel Bell, in the third round of this year's draft.

Bell started Sunday in place of Johnson and played all 61 offensive snaps in the 24-20 loss to the Rams. He recovered a fumble after Jalen Hurts was strip-sacked and drew one illegal formation penalty.

Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion said Bell has "been working his tail off" and "ready to go all year."

"By no means did he play a perfect game, but he did some really good things," Sirianni told reporters on Monday. "I think that watching the tape with the team today, with some of the things that we show, he got some really good movement on some double teams and second level stuff that we were able to show and highlight and point out for his teammates to see. Like anybody in this game of football, you never pitch a perfect game. There are things that we got to correct as well.

What will Philadelphia miss without Johnson moving forward?

When the Eagles face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday morning, they'll do so with several offensive injuries and now a depth drop at right tackle.

Even at 36 years old this season, Johnson ranked among the best offensive tackles in pass blocking. Johnson won 92% of his pass-block sets (73 of 79) through three weeks, per ESPN's pass-block win rate metric , second in the league only to the Las Vegas Raiders' Kolton Miller. He won 92% of the time despite facing double teams on 49% of his sets.

Opponents knew his 6-6, 325-pound frame and 35 1/4 -inch arms, per his scouting combine measurements, created a length-athleticism combination difficult to thwart.

"Seemed like he was the first 'right tackle with true left tackle traits,'" one defensive coach who faced Johnson recently told Yahoo Sports on condition of anonymity. "Seemed like the Eagles and Lane were trendsetters in terms of valuing the right tackle. Typically, top right tackles were better run blockers than pass blockers.

Tuesday, Johnson announced his intentions were different than they'd been to start the season. After telling reporters during training camp that he planned to finish out this season, his emotions and priorities shifted.

"I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season," Johnson said in a statement. "But after a lot of reflection, I've realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed. Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health.

"I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game. And right now my heart is telling me that it's time to say goodbye to football."

articles.title: Eagles OT Lane Johnson announces retirement after decorated 14-year NFL career
articles.summary: Johnson missed the Eagles' Week 4 game due to "personal reasons."
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Lane Johnson announced his retirement on Tuesday.

Johnson was a surprise inactive for the Eagles' Week 4 game and was cited as not playing for personal reasons.

The offensive lineman spent 14 seasons with the Eagles and won two Super Bowls.

Johnson, 36, has mulled retirement over the last few seasons. The lineman has long been a big advocate for mental health, so he always checked that he and his family could handle continuing his career in both areas.

Johnson played the first three weeks of the season, but has decided it is time to hang up his cleats. He'd previously said this would likely be the final season of his career, but said in a statement he was unable to finish out the season.

"I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season," Johnson said. "But after a lot of reflection, I've realized that my personal and family priorities in my life have changed. Right now, it is critical that I focus on my mental health."

The Eagles released a statement supporting Johnson and his decision.

Johnson eventually is expected to be inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame once he qualifies in five years. He was a quarterback in junior college and even when he first arrived at the University of Oklahoma, according to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer .

He then switched to tight end, before finally converting to offensive line. Philadelphia drafted Johnson with the fourth overall pick in the 2013 NFL Draft.

The offensive lineman ends his career as a six-time Pro Bowler and two-time First Team All-Pro.

With Johnson stepping away from football, the Eagles will look to try to replicate his production on the line. Philadelphia is already down Landon Dickerson, who has been on injured reserve since Week 1.

The Eagles' projected offensive line for now features standouts Jordan Mailata and Cam Jurgens, alongside Drew Kendall, Tyler Steen and Fred Johnson (no relation to Lane).

Philly has developed offensive line talent in the past and needs Kendall, Steen, and Fred Johnson to step up. This all comes at a time when Philadelphia's offense is struggling amid injuries to receiver DeVonta Smith, tight end Dallas Goedert and running backs Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby.

The Eagles will miss Lane Johnson's production, though. According to Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein , the Eagles are 112-58-1 since drafting him in 2013. Philly is 18-28 in games he has missed.

articles.title: Winners and Losers from Cowboys big win over Texans
articles.summary: The biggest winners and losers after the Cowboys 34-30 come from behind victory over the Texans in dramatic fashion
articles.body:
The Cowboys came away with a dramatic 34-30 come-from-behind victory over a desperate Houston Texans team giving Dallas a reason to be optimistic moving forward.

Not every performance was created equal though as several players stepped up when their opportunities arrived while others struggled to make the kind of impact that is expected from them.

Just missing the cut, Tyler Guyton has grown into a legitimate left tackle and is no longer a problem for Dallas while safety Caleb Downs continues to be a bright spot on defense. On the other hand, tight end Jake Ferguson's run blocking effort continues to garner collective eye rolls and sighs.

As is often the case following a hard-fought game, the final result may have been positive, but individual stock certainly moved in different directions. Here are the biggest winners and losers from a game that could prove pivotal as Dallas continues to shape their season.

Breaking the Cowboys All-Time single game reception record for a wide receiver while catching the go-ahead game winning touchdown is a signature moment in what has been an outstanding start to the season for wideout CeeDee Lamb.

Only Cowboys tight end Jason Witten, with 18 receptions back in 2012, has ever caught more passes in a game for the Cowboys but that still doesn't damper the performance Lamb displayed against what was the best defense in the NFL last season.

SuperLamb finished with 189 receiving yards to go along with the aforementioned TD to essentially save the Cowboys from dwelling in the NFC East basement. The seventh-year wide receiver was unguardable against the Texans whose vaunted defense had no answers.

He now has 37 receptions for 498 receiving yards on the year which are both tops in the NFL, to go along with four touchdowns marking the best start to his career after four games.

Lamb is on pace for 157 receptions which would break Michael Thomas' record when he caught 149 passes for the Saints back in 2019. Lamb is also on pace for 2,116 receiving yards which would shatter Calvin Johnson's record of 1,964 yards set back during the 2012 season for Detroit.

No player has ever recorded 2,000 receiving yards in NFL history and Lamb would need to average 115.5 yards a game for the rest of the season to reach that mark but L2K does have a nice ring to it.

Loser - Nick Sorenesen - Special Teams Coordinator

While the Cowboys defense has eaten up much of the headlines for their porous start to the season, the Dallas special teams units have continued their downward trend which may have hit a point where a conversation might have to be had about special teams coordinator Nick Sorensen.

Replaced after one season as the 49ers defensive coordinator, Sorensen latched on with Dallas last season taking over for the insightful and innovative John "Bones" Fassel, and things in Dallas have stagnated.

Dallas had a Brandon Aubrey FG attempt blocked after the Texans detected an issue with the Cowboys blocking scheme by overloading one side.

The Cowboys have now had kicks blocked in back-to-back games for the first time since 1991 and almost had another blocked by Texans edge Will Anderson which could have altered Houstons approach towards the end of the game.

Dallas gave up 161 kick return yards on seven attempts against Houston. Last season, the Dallas kickoff unit gave up 2,097 yards — second most in the NFL only to the Jets. That number is more than Fassel's units gave up in his final three seasons in Dallas combined (2,010).

With 422 yards allowed through four games, Dallas is doing better than last season but is still on pace to give up 1,793 kick return yards.

If things continue to falter, an in-season coaching change must be considered as giving short fields to offenses hurts the defenses chances of improving as the season continues to unfold.

The overall statistics may not stand out on paper but the impact running back Javonte Williams had en route to a hat-trick was only visible to those who watched the game.

Williams finished the game with 19 carries for 62 yards, good for an average of 3.2 yards per rush, yet his three touchdown scores were key in the Cowboys keeping pace in the division and also perhaps the conference.

Williams now has 16 rushing touchdowns since signing with Dallas prior to the 2025 season and marks the third time he has scored multiple rushing TD's since joining the team. His three scores are the most he's ever had in a game in his NFL career.

His ability to pick up blitzes or help chip defenders allowed QB Dak Prescott to stand in the pocket and ease the harassment usually bestowed by the Texans defense. According to PFF, Williams has allowed just one QB hit on 42 pass blocking attempts this season with no sacks or hurries allowed.

The Cowboys defense showed signs of improvement including two, three-&-out's while holding Houston to 3-of-10 on third down but issues remain — namely, cover corners DaRon Bland and Reddy Steward.

Bland was given a four-year, $92 million contract extension to be the teams top cornerback and the deal appears to be an overpay or perhaps compensation for services already rendered. Either way, Bland is not living up to his contract status and his future with the team will come in to question until his performances improve.

According to PFF, Bland allowed five receptions on seven targets for 104 yards. Houston shied away from the newly acquired Joey Porter Jr. and opted to pick on the teams highest paid defensive back instead. Yuck.

Steward was also picked on allowing three receptions for 48 yards according to PFF. The miscommunication between him and Bland on the first play of the game allowed Texans WR Nico Collins to run open for a 45-yard reception.

Collins would cap the opening drive beating Bland for a seven-yard TD reception — Houstons' first opening drive points of the season.

Luckily for Dallas, reinforcements should steadily return as a rash of injuries have forced Dallas to give snaps to players who did not make the initial 53-man roster which is affecting the cohesion and familiarity of a new defensive system.

Quarterback Dak Prescott didn't have the best starts to the game against a stingy Houston defense but showed all the reasons why keeping the game close late in games gives the Cowboys a punchers chance.

He now has 27 game-winning drives and the victory tied him with Hall-of-Fame quarterback Roger Staubach for second place All-Time for most regular-season wins by a Cowboys quarterback with 85 victories.

Prescott finished going 32 of 45 for 335 yards and a game winning touchdown pass to Lamb.

Prescott ranks sixth in passing yards with 1,065 and eight TD passes, third in completions with 105, and is tied with San Francisco for second place averaging 30.5 points per game.

His lone interception came on an attempted throw away pass against the Giants in Week 1.

While the ultimate goal is for Dallas to win a championship, individually, Prescott should be in the MVP conversation as long as the teams record can coincide with his current performance.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer started the week apologizing to his players and taking the blame for his decision-making at the end of the Ravens contest that cost the team a win but his issues remain despite his players bailing him out of another question filled contest.

Towards the end of the first half, Schotty opted to attempt a 65-yard field goal instead of punting and pinning the Texans back with seconds left until halftime. Kicker Brandon Aubrey missed the field goal giving Houston great field position which resulted in the Texans putting up three points and ended the half up 16-6.

His insistence on not running ball while close to the goal line, attempting to block edge players with TE Jake Ferguson, and a questionable organizational challenge process officially marks the end of the honeymoon phase in Dallas.

The first time, second-year head coach must be the catalyst for his team winning as opposed a roadblock for their losses. Continued success often masks glaring issues but Schotty must be better moving forward.

Luckily for him, Dallas has a short week against a wounded opponent at home that could vault them to the top of the division standings all while looking ahead at a schedule that could see them never relinquish the lead.

You can follow Angel on X @ArmyChiefW3 and be sure to follow Cowboys Wire on Facebook to join in on the conversation with fellow fans!

articles.title: Eagles RB depth chart: Will Shipley poised to play big role after Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby injuries
articles.summary: Here's the latest on the Eagles' RB depth chart after Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby were cut down with injuries.
articles.body:
Four weeks into the 2026 season, one thing has been laid abundantly clear: the Eagles attack looks far less high-powered than it once appeared.

Nick Sirianni's side has struggled to produce points in recent weeks. In Week 3, Philadelphia mustered a single touchdown en route to defeat against the Bears . One week later, the Eagles' offensive torpidity resurfaced — Philadelphia finished with fewer than 200 yards of total offense for just the second time in five seasons.

Much of those toils stem from injuries. Devonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley have been stricken by poor health as of late, leaving them off the field for the time being.

Barkley's absence, in particular, could prove devastating, especially given Philly's lack of depth in that position.

With that, here's what you need to know about the state of the Eagles' RB room after injuries swept through their ranks.

The injuries continue to pile up in Philadelphia's backfield. Barkley left the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams prematurely with a hamstring injury. The ailment isn't expected to keep him out for long; according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport, Barkley is considered week-to-week with the ailment. He could struggle to be ruled fit in time to take part in the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jaguars in London.

Bigsby had emerged as Philadelphia's RB2, fielding the lion's share of snaps after Barkley exited the game. He, too, was cut down by injury on Sunday, though, sustaining an injury to his core. He'll undergo surgery to repair an issue with one of his muscles and head to the injured reserve list.

With Barkley and Bigsby on the mend, that leaves only third-stringer Will Shipley to field carries in Week 5. The Clemson product has featured sparingly since entering the league, only amassing 182 yards across three seasons. He has never amassed more than 10 carries in a game and has failed to find the end zone yet in the regular season.

Despite the uncertainty surrounding his viability, Philadelphia has few other options to go to after Barkley and Bigsby's injuries. The franchise doesn't even have a running back listed on its practice squad.

Assuming the organization doesn't try to rush Barkley back in Week 5, things could look a little scarce for the Eagles' RB room on the other side of the pond.

articles.title: Vikings Add Christian Darrisaw Roster Replacement, Cut All-Pro in Major Shake-Up
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings moved several parts around on their roster, including adding a roster replacement for Christian Darrisaw. The post Vikings Add Christia...
articles.body:
Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings made several roster moves on the eve of their first practice in Week 5 (and their upcoming matchup against the New Orleans Saints), including adding Tristan Leigh and moving on from Johnny Hekker.

"The #Vikings have announced the following roster moves," the team announced in a post on X on October 5:

Signed T Tristan Leigh to the practice squad

Released CB Natrone Brooks, P Johnny Hekker and RB Devin Neal from the practice squad

O'Connell announced that Jackson was undergoing surgery for a torn meniscus and would miss the rest of the 2026 season on Monday. The Vikings will also not have left tackle Christian Darrisaw in Week 5.

Leigh is not a direct replacement for Darrisaw. However, he does replenish the depth they will not tap into for at least Week 5 and could replace Darrisaw on the game-day roster in Week 5.

"Leigh needs added technical refinement, but he utilizes quality angles in pass protection to cut off rush angles, and he leans on defenders in the run game," The Athletic's Dane Brugler wrote before the 2026 draft. "He is a potential depth piece for an NFL offensive line room."

NFL.com's Lance Zierlein wrote in his pre-draft write-up, "Former five-star recruit with good length and athletic ability but inconsistencies that could hurt his chances on the next level. Leigh has the footwork and hand-timing for protection success in the early stages of the rep but struggles anchoring against power. He gets into trouble with excessive lunging.

"Quick out of his stance and is able to hit lateral/second-level landmarks but his lack of sustain strength will be hard for him to overcome as a run blocker."

Texans Cutting Ties With Johnny Hekker, Four Others Amid Tristan Leigh Roster Move

Leigh was the Vikings' only addition, and Jackson their only player landing on an injured list at this time.

The Vikings initially signed Hekker to fill in for an injured Brett Thorson. Hekker is a Super Bowl champion with the Los Angeles Rams in 2021. He has multiple Pro Bowls and First Team All-Pro honors on his resume. He punted in Weeks 3 and 4 for the Vikings.

His departure could signal that Thorson is ready to resume his duties as P1.

Brooks and Neal are both recent additions made in the wake of injuries to players already on the Vikings' roster.

Brooks was brought on after Charles Demmings suffered a hamstring injury that sidelined him in Week 4. Vikings running back Aaron Jones shed his injury designation heading into Sunday's tilt. They also signed Audric Estime to the practice squad , eliminating the need for Neal .

Because he is being waived from IR, that likely means the transaction involved an injury settlement.

If so, Chappell can sign with any of the 31 other NFL teams right away. If he wants to return to the Vikings, and if they want him back, he must wait for the duration of his settlement agreement plus an additional time (typically three weeks).
